exercises.heading: 12.4. Exercises
exercises.instruction: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 Find the cross product $$\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}$$ and verify that it is orthogonal to both $$\mathbf{a}$$ and $$\mathbf{b}$$ .

problem.paragraph: If $$\mathbf{a} = \mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{k}$$ and $$\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}$$ , find $$\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}$$ . Sketch $$\mathbf{a}$$ , $$\mathbf{b}$$ , and $$\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}$$ as vectors starting at the origin.

exercises.instruction: 9, 10, 11, and 12 Find the vector, not with determinants, but by using properties of cross products.

problem.paragraph: State whether each expression is meaningful. If not, explain why. If so, state whether it is a vector or a scalar.

exercises.instruction: 14–15 Find $$\left| {\mathbf{u} \times \mathbf{v}} \right|$$ and determine whether $$\mathbf{u} \times \mathbf{v}$$ is directed into the page or out of the page.

problem.paragraph: 14. Details Two vectors are displayed, both starting from a common point. The first vector points vertically downward and is labeled abs(v) = 8. The second vector slopes downward to the right, at an angle of 60 degrees from the first and is labeled abs(u) = 10.

15. Details Two vectors are displayed, both starting from a common point The first vector, points horizontally rightward and is labeled abs(u) = 4. The second vector slopes downward to the right, at an angle of 150 degrees from the first, and is labeled abs(v) = 3. $$6$$ ; into the page

The figure shows a vector $$\mathbf{a}$$ in the $$\mathit{xy}$$ -plane and a vector $$\mathbf{b}$$ in the direction of $$\mathbf{k}$$ . Their lengths are $$\left| \mathbf{a} \right| = 3$$ and $$\left| \mathbf{b} \right| = 2$$ .

list.item: Use the right-hand rule to decide whether the components of $$\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}$$ are positive, negative, or $$0$$ . Details Two vectors are graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. The first vector, labeled vector a lies on the x y plane. The second vector, labeled vector b, runs vertically upward, along the positive z axis.

problem.paragraph: Find two unit vectors orthogonal to both $$\langle{3,2,1}\rangle$$ and $$\langle{- 1,1,0}\rangle$$ .
Find two unit vectors orthogonal to both $$\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}$$ and $$\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j}$$ .
Show that $$0 \times \mathbf{a} = 0 = \mathbf{a} \times 0$$ for any vector $$\mathbf{a}$$ in $$V_{3}$$ .
Show that $$\left( {\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}} \right) \cdot \mathbf{b} = 0$$ for all vectors $$\mathbf{a}$$ and $$\mathbf{b}$$ in $$V_{3}$$ .

exercises.instruction: 23, 24, 25, and 26 Prove the specified property of cross products (Theorem 11).

problem.paragraph: Find the area of the parallelogram with vertices $$A\left( {- 3,0} \right)$$ , $$B\left( {- 1,3} \right)$$ , $$C\left( {5,2} \right)$$ , and $$D\left( {3, - 1} \right)$$ .
Find the area of the parallelogram with vertices $$P\left( {1,0,2} \right)$$ , $$Q\left( {3,3,3} \right)$$ , $$R\left( {7,5,8} \right)$$ , and $$S\left( {5,2,7} \right)$$ .

exercises.instruction: 29, 30, 31, and 32 Find a nonzero vector orthogonal to the plane through the points $$P$$ , $$Q$$ , and $$R$$ , and find the area of triangle $$PQR$$ .
33–34 Find the volume of the parallelepiped determined by the vectors $$\mathbf{a}$$ , $$\mathbf{b}$$ , and $$\mathbf{c}$$ .
35–36 Find the volume of the parallelepiped with adjacent edges $$\mathit{PQ}$$ , $$\mathit{PR}$$ , and $$\mathit{PS}$$ .

problem.paragraph: Use the scalar triple product to verify that the vectors $$\mathbf{u} = \mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j} - 2\mathbf{k}$$ , $$\mathbf{v} = 3\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j}$$ , and $$\mathbf{w} = 5\mathbf{i} + 9\mathbf{j} - 4\mathbf{k}$$ are coplanar.

Use the scalar triple product to determine whether the points $$A\left( {1,3,2} \right)$$ , $$B\left( {3, - 1,6} \right)$$ , $$C\left( {5,2,0} \right)$$ , and $$D\left( {3,6, - 4} \right)$$ lie in the same plane.
A bicycle pedal is pushed by a foot with a $$60$$ -N force as shown in the figure. The shaft of the pedal is $$18$$ cm long. Find the magnitude of the torque about $$P$$ .

image.alt: Details The figure shows a two dimensional rendering of a pedal and its shaft. The pedal is on the left and is horizontal. From the top of the pedal, a horizontal dashed line extends rightward. A vector, labeled 60 newton's, slopes downward to the left and acts on the center of the pedal at an angle of 70 degrees from the dashed line. The shaft slopes downward to the right from the pedal at an angle 10 degrees from the dashed line and meets a bolt, labeled P.

list.item: A horizontal force of $$20$$ lb is applied to the handle of a gearshift lever as shown in the figure. Find the magnitude of the torque about the pivot point $$P$$ . Details The figure displays a two dimensional rendering of a gearshift. The gear shift has a circular head, labeled P, an elbow formed by a bent beam. The beam begins at P slopes upward to the right as it tapers and then slopes steeply upward to the right and ends with a handle. At the center of the bend, a point is labeled Q. A horizontal vector from the center of the handle extends rightward and is labeled 20 pounds. The vertical distance between P and the handle is 2 feet. The vertical distance between P and Q is 0.6 feet. The horizontal distance between P and the handle is 1 foot. The horizontal distance between P and Q is 0.6 feet.
Find the magnitude of the torque about $$P$$ if the same force is applied at the elbow $$Q$$ of the lever.

problem.paragraph: A wrench $$30$$ cm long lies along the positive $$y$$ -axis and grips a bolt at the origin. A force is applied in the direction $$\langle{0,3, - 4}\rangle$$ at the end of the wrench. Find the magnitude of the force needed to supply $$100N \cdot m$$ of torque to the bolt.

Let $$\mathbf{v} = 5\mathbf{j}$$ and let $$\mathbf{u}$$ be a vector with length $$3$$ that starts at the origin and rotates in the $$\mathit{xy}$$ -plane. Find the maximum and minimum values of the length of the vector $$\mathbf{u} \times \mathbf{v}$$ . In what direction does $$\mathbf{u} \times \mathbf{v}$$ point?
If $$\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = \sqrt{3}$$ and $$\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} = {\langle{1,2,2}\rangle}$$ , find the angle between $$\mathbf{a}$$ and $$\mathbf{b}$$ .

list.item: Explain why there is no vector $$\mathbf{v}$$ such that $${\langle{1,2,1}\rangle} \times \mathbf{v} = {\langle{3,1,5}\rangle}$$

problem.paragraph: Distance from a Point to a Line Let $$P$$ be a point not on the line $$L$$ that passes through the points $$Q$$ and $$R$$ .

list.item: Show that the distance $$d$$ from the point $$P$$ to the line $$L$$ is $$d = \frac{\left| {\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}} \right|}{\left| \mathbf{a} \right|}$$ where $$\mathbf{a} = \overset{\rightarrow}{\mathit{QR}}$$ and $$\mathbf{b} = \overset{\rightarrow}{\mathit{QP}}$$ .
Use the formula in part (a) to find the distance from the point $$P\left( {1,1,1} \right)$$ to the line through $$Q\left( {0,6,8} \right)$$ and $$R\left( {- 1,4,7} \right)$$ .

problem.paragraph: Distance from a Point to a Plane Let $$P$$ be a point not on the plane that passes through the points $$Q$$ , $$R$$ , and $$S$$ .

list.item: Show that the distance $$d$$ from $$P$$ to the plane is $$d = \frac{\left| {\mathbf{a} \cdot \left( {\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}} \right)} \right|}{\left| {\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}} \right|}$$ where $$\mathbf{a} = \overset{\rightarrow}{\mathit{QR}}$$ , $$\mathbf{b} = \overset{\rightarrow}{\mathit{QS}}$$ , and $$\mathbf{c} = \overset{\rightarrow}{\mathit{QP}}$$ .

Use the formula in part (a) to find the distance from the point $$P\left( {2,1,4} \right)$$ to the plane through the points $$Q\left( {1,0,0} \right)$$ , $$R\left( {0,2,0} \right)$$ , and $$S\left( {0,0,3} \right)$$ .

problem.paragraph: Prove Property 6 of cross products, that is,

list.item: If $$\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{c}$$ and $$\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{c}$$ , does it follow that $$\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{c}$$ ?

problem.paragraph: If $$\mathbf{v}_{1}$$ , $$\mathbf{v}_{2}$$ , and $$\mathbf{v}_{3}$$ are noncoplanar vectors, let

(These vectors occur in the study of crystallography. Vectors of the form $$n_{1}\mathbf{v}_{1} + n_{2}\mathbf{v}_{2} + n_{3}\mathbf{v}_{3}$$ , where each $$n_{i}$$ is an integer, form a lattice for a crystal. Vectors written similarly in terms of $$\mathbf{k}_{1}$$ , $$\mathbf{k}_{2}$$ , and $$\mathbf{k}_{3}$$ form the reciprocal lattice.)

list.item: Show that $$\mathbf{k}_{i}$$ is perpendicular to $$\mathbf{v}_{j}$$ if $$i \neq j$$ .
